heroText: Budapest is a Danube capital of thermal baths, grand cafes, ruin bars and hilltop views. Start at Buda Castle, cross the Chain Bridge area, then plan Parliament, the Jewish Quarter and Széchenyi Thermal Bath across different parts of the city. Budapest Airport is southeast of town, with bus and taxi transfers into the centre.

areas.name: District V
areas.text: District V is the central Pest base for Parliament, river walks, shopping streets and classic first visits.

areas.name: Jewish Quarter
areas.text: The Jewish Quarter is lively, with ruin bars, restaurants, synagogues and strong nightlife access.

areas.name: Buda Castle District
areas.text: Buda Castle District is quieter and historic, with views and atmosphere but fewer late-night options.

areas.name: Terézváros
areas.text: Terézváros suits Opera, Andrassy Avenue, transport and a balance of hotels and local streets.

airports.text: Budapest Airport is southeast of the city, with airport buses, taxis and transfers into central Pest.

airportTransfer.note: from Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport

stayOverview: District V is the easiest first base, the Jewish Quarter is best for nightlife, Buda Castle District is quieter and scenic, and Terézváros balances culture, transport and hotel choice.
hotelIntro: Budapest is split by the Danube. Pest is usually better for restaurants and nightlife, while Buda suits views and calmer historic stays if you accept more climbing or transit.
rentalCars: Do not rent for Budapest; public transport, walking and trains are better for the city and common day trips.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose District V for a first visit, or the Jewish Quarter if ruin bars and restaurants are the focus.

travelTips.title: Baths
travelTips.text: Keep the Budapest plan compact: group nearby sights together and leave enough time for transfers, meals and weather changes.

travelTips.title: Transit
travelTips.text: Use BKK passes for metro, trams and buses; tram rides along the Danube are especially useful.

travelTips.title: Day trip
travelTips.text: Keep one side-trip day flexible from Budapest, then choose it only after checking transport frequency and opening hours.

history.text: The Roman settlement – Aquincum – became the main city of Pannonia Inferior in 106 AD.

history.label: 11th century
history.text: Buda was probably the name of the first constable of the fortress built on the Castle Hill in the 11th century or a derivative of Bod or Bud, a personal name of Turkic origin.
In 1361 it became the capital of Hungary.
After the foundation of the first Hungarian university in Pécs in 1367 (University of Pécs), the second one was established in Óbuda in 1395 (University of Óbuda).
In the 1699 Treaty of Karlowitz, these territorial changes were officially recognized as the end of the rule of the Turks, and in 1718 the entire Kingdom of Hungary was removed from Ottoman rule.

history.label: 19th century
history.text: Budapest also became an important center for the Aromanian diaspora during the 19th century.
The national insurrection against the Habsburgs began in the Hungarian capital in 1848 and was defeated one and a half years later, with the help of the Russian Empire.
Between 1851 and 1910 the proportion of Hungarians increased from 35.6% to 85.9%, Hungarian became the dominant language, and German was crowded out.
In 1944, a year before the end of World War II, Budapest was partly destroyed by British and American air raids (first attack 4 April 1944).

history.label: 1950s
history.text: The new Communist government considered the buildings like the Buda Castle symbols of the former regime, and during the 1950s the palace was gutted and all the interiors were destroyed (also see Stalin era).
Work on Erzsébet Bridge, the last to be rebuilt, was finished in 1964.

history.label: 1970s
history.text: In the early 1970s, Budapest Metro's east–west M2 line was first opened, followed by the M3 line in 1976.
Andrássy Avenue (including the Millennium Underground Railway, Hősök tere, and Városliget) was added to the UNESCO list in 2002.
